subject: Clarify: BYOK / audit exports scope and delivery for MedSpring

Subject: BYOK / audit exports — specific asks and timeline

Hi Laura,

Thanks for the quick onboarding call earlier. Procurement and security asked me to follow up with a concise list of what we need to close the SOW and prove compliance for our integrations team. High level:

- BYOK/KMS: confirmation on whether Redwood Hosted customers can have tenant-specific CMKs (we understand Dedicated or Private may differ). If not possible, please call out the options and timelines.
- Audit exports: sample of audit logs for a single tenant (showing API request trace, token-level metadata, SSO events) and a CSV schema for exported fields.
- Retention windows: default retention for audit logs, and options for short-window temporary retention (30/90/180 days).
- Evidence pack: what formal artifacts you can provide (SOC2 excerpts, signed statements, sample logs) and expected delivery time.

I'm attaching our security questionnaire and a one-page vendor checklist. Can you route to whoever owns BYOK/KMS and audit exports? We need to close the procurement thread by 2026-07-20 to hit our implementation start date.

Subject: Re: BYOK / audit exports — specific asks and timeline

Thanks for the ping, Laura — looping in my notes after a quick triage with infra. Short answers first:

- BYOK / CMK: Hosted (multi-tenant) customers cannot currently provision tenant-specific CMKs for model payload encryption or tracing keys. BYOK is supported on Dedicated and Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem). We can provide a documented exception path but that requires Legal + Infra sign-off and an SRE-run configuration (non-trivial).

- Audit exports (today): we can produce per-tenant exported audit records covering API request metadata, auth events (SSO), and model selection. The export is currently a manual job (SRE-run) that pulls from our internal telemetry for a requested window. Schema: timestamp, request_id, tenant_id (hashed), api_endpoint, model, response_latency_ms, user_agent, auth_method, sso_event_type (login/logout), token_bearer_hash. We'll attach a sanitized sample.

- Retention windows: primary telemetry store retains event-level logs for 180 days. We keep aggregate telemetry and metrics longer (24 months) but detailed request traces beyond 180 days require an exported snapshot or cold-archive request. For short-window temporary retention (e.g., 30 days), we can provide a contractually-scoped export and hold it in escrow for the requested period.

Action items / proposed plan:
1) Security (me) will prepare the sanitized audit sample and the export schema doc — ETA: 3 business days (2026-07-14 EOD).
2) Infra (Priyom) to confirm effort for a one-off tenant export and time to run (estimate 1–2 business days once authorized). Also outline any access controls for the output.
3) Product (Marissa) to advise whether we want to accelerate a small Console feature to add a one-click evidence export for Tier-1 customers (if procurement asks become frequent). Rough estimate: 6–8 sprint-weeks to deliver minimally.
4) Sales (Laura) to confirm MedSpring's hard deadline (Laura: 2026-07-20) and whether they'd accept the manual evidence pack now + roadmap commitment for self-serve later.

Constraints / risks:
- Hosted BYOK would be an architectural change; cannot be promised for this procurement cycle.
- Audit exports contain sensitive metadata; we need an approved NDAs and procurement PO before running exports.

I'll start with the sanitized sample and put it in the secure drive link.

— Jonas Weber
Head of Security Engineering
jonas.weber@redwood.ai
From: marissa.cole@redwood.ai <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: laura.bennett@redwood.ai, jonas.weber@redwood.ai, priyom.das@redwood.ai
Cc: irene.choi@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 12 Jul 2026 08:21:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: BYOK / audit exports — specific asks and timeline

Thanks — quick product take and suggested customer-facing options. I tried to keep the language procurement-friendly.

Option A (short term, recommended): manual evidence pack
- What: Security prepares sanitized audit export and a one-page statement (signed) about retention and export process. Infra runs a one-off export and deposits a tarball in a secure bucket.
- Pros: fast, low engineering effort (SRE + security owner).
- Cons: manual and not scalable; SRE time per customer.
- ETA: 5 business days from authorization.

Option B (medium term): Console evidence export beta (Tier-1 customers)
- What: small Console feature to request an evidence export from the UI, gated by role/contract. Backend will invoke an export job and put artifacts into a customer-accessible folder.
- Pros: repeatable, reduces SRE friction, better audit trail.
- Cons: ~6–8 sprints, needs product + infra prioritization.

Option C (long term): hosted BYOK for multi-tenant customers — needs architectural investment and legal changes. Not feasible as a short-term promise.

Requested guidance from Sales: if MedSpring accepts Option A from a contractual standpoint, we will commit to Option B timeline evaluation in the next roadmap review and provide an estimated delivery quarter.

Technical notes for docs: ensure export schema masks PII and uses tenant_id hash; include a signed statement about log retention policy (180d) and export custody.

— Marissa Cole
Director, Product Management
marissa.cole@redwood.ai

Hi Claire / Tom — thanks for the clear list. Short summary and next steps from our side:

1) Delivered items (this week):
- Jonas will deliver a sanitized audit sample and the export schema by 2026-07-14 EOD (we will put the files in the secure Drive folder and share a link).
- Attached: signed NDA (MedSpring_NDA_signed.pdf) — thank you for sending this over.

2) Hosted BYOK: not available for Hosted multi-tenant customers today. BYOK is supported on Dedicated and Private. If BYOK for Hosted is a gating requirement, we need to evaluate Dedicated/private routes (we can provide a cost + timeline separately).

3) Retention & exports: default detailed event retention is 180 days. We can produce a contract-scoped export and hold it in escrow for a specified short-window (30/90/180 days) if needed for your audit.

4) Proposed immediate path (to meet your 2026-07-20 procurement date):
- Approve the manual evidence pack (Option A). We will require a PO + signed evidence handling agreement (we've attached our template in the Drive link).
- Security (Jonas) + Infra (Priyom) will run the export once procurement provides formal authorization and the PO. Expected delivery: 1–3 business days after authorization.

5) Roadmap follow-up: Product suggests evaluating a Console export feature (Option B). We will provide an internal estimate and a target quarter for a beta in the next roadmap review.

Can you confirm that MedSpring will accept Option A as a near-term deliverable? If yes, please reply with a formal authorization (procurement PO or email approval) and we will kick the export.
